newsitem.title: CHINA: China says wants end to U.N. sanctions against Iraq.
newsitem.headline: China says wants end to U.N. sanctions against Iraq.

text.p: China wants to see an end to U.N. sanctions against Iraq as soon as possible, Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen told visiting Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz on Monday.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin also met Aziz and told him that maintaining contacts between Chinese and Iraqi leaders was conducive to enhancing mutual understanding and cooperation.
Jiang expressed sympathy for the Iraqi people in their suffering from the sanctions, the official Xinhua news agency said.
China has long maintained that it wants to see a lifting of the sanctions, imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Diplomats said the visit by Aziz was almost certainly aimed at nurturing support from China in the U.N. Security Council.

Beijing may also be keen to see an end to the sanctions that would enable it to go ahead with a deal in principle between China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) and Iraq to develop the 80,000 barrel per day (bpd) al-Ahdab and 250,000 bpd Halfaya oil fields.
No final deal could be signed until the sanctions were lifted, a CNPC official said, adding that no concrete progress was expected during Aziz's visit.
"The settlement of the problems at an earlier date is in the fundamental interests of the people in the Gulf region, and the peace, stability, and unity in the region," Xinhua quoted Qian as saying.

The U.N. curbs include a ban on Baghdad's oil exports that will not be lifted until the U.N. Special Commission -- the body in charge of disarming Iraq -- testifies that Baghdad has no more weapons of mass destruction.
The United Nations has, however, allowed Iraq since December to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for Iraqis suffering from the sanctions.
China appreciated Iraq's stand of continuing cooperation with the United Nations, and hoped U.N. departments would accelerate the process of inspecting Iraq's arsenal, Qian said.

He said he also hoped the United Nations would "objectively and justly appraise Iraq's efforts to carry out relevant resolutions of the U.N. Security Council in order to ease and gradually lift the sanctions on Iraq", Xinhua said.
China wanted to advance ties with all Arab nations, Qian said.

Aziz said he hoped China, as a permanent member of the U.N. Security Council, would play an active role in the council in making contributions to the peace and stability in the Gulf region, Xinhua reported.
